**17 call sites** still pass the legacy rounding flag, across **7 files**. (The 18th match is the definition itself in `src/lib/format.js:6`.)

| File | Two-arg calls |
|---|---|
| `src/reports/quarterly.js` | **5** |
| `src/admin/exports.js` | 3 |
| `src/billing/invoice.js` | 3 |
| `src/checkout/cart.js` | 2 |
| `src/reports/monthly.js` | 2 |
| `src/billing/statement.js` | 1 |
| `src/checkout/receipt.js` | 1 |

`src/reports/quarterly.js` has the most, with 5 (lines 16, 37, 58, 83, 104).

Notes from the sweep:

- Every one of the 17 passes the literal `true` — there are no `false` or variable-valued second args, so no call site is silently a no-op that you could delete for free. All 17 are behavior-carrying.
- Four other files use `formatAmount` but are already fully migrated to the one-arg form: `src/admin/dashboard.js`, `src/reports/ledger.js`, `src/billing/refunds.js`, and `src/checkout/receipt.js` (1 remaining call there).
- Dropping the flag isn't purely mechanical: per `src/lib/format.js:3-16`, `true` rounds half away from zero while the default rounds half to even. The two differ only on exact `.005` midpoints, but for money that's a real output change at those 17 sites.
